Hi Alex —

Thanks again for choosing Redwood. To make the first-week hookup smooth, I put together the initial asks and a proposed sequence for project seeding, admin invites, and an "API escrow" option you asked about. Attachment: access-matrix.xlsx and mutual_action_plan.md.

Quick asks for kickoff call (can be 30 min):
- Confirm project name you want us to seed (recommended: brightbridge-prod / brightbridge-staging)
- List of 2 admin users to receive console-level invites
- Primary SRE/service account email for API key consumption/rotation
- Any requirement to use your KMS/HSM vs Redwood-managed encrypted escrow

High-level sequence I propose:
1) We seed a staging project and create a staging API key for testing.
2) Your admins confirm roles & run smoke tests.
3) We seed production project and create a production key to be escrowed. Options: customer-managed key (you keep the KMS/HSM), or Redwood escrow with customer key-wrap and automatic rotation (we can provide rotation cadence).
4) After validation, production key is activated and rotated according to agreed cadence.

Please reply with the three bullets above and a couple 30-min slots for a kickoff this week.

Regards,
Soojin Lee

Hi Alex —

Great — 10:00am PT tomorrow works for our team; I’ll send a calendar invite.

Short answers:
- API escrow: we offer two patterns. 1) Customer-managed: you generate keys in your KMS/HSM and grant Redwood a wrapped key for runtime; you retain ultimate control and can rotate without Redwood access. 2) Redwood-managed escrow: we store the production key encrypted with a customer-supplied key-encryption-key (KEK) or with Redwood KMS and provide an agreed rotation schedule and access controls/audit logs. The mutual_action_plan.md has both flows spelled out.
- Admin auth: SAML SSO is preferred for enterprise teams; we also support invite+MFA for initial seeding if you prefer. For long-term, we recommend SAML with SCIM provisioning where possible.

For the kickoff agenda I’ll cover: invite sequence, project naming & quotas, API key scoping & rotation, and SOC2/data handling notes. Monica (CS implementation lead) and Dev will cover the admin seed & technical checklist.

Attaching the MAP link in chat and copying key excerpts below.

Regards,
Soojin

Alex / team —

Adding the technical checklist we’ll use during the kickoff and the seeding sprint:

- Project & naming: brightbridge-staging / brightbridge-prod. Please confirm tenant ID format (we’ll create project ids like bb-<shorthash>).
- Admin roles: two console admins (Owner role) + one billing contact (no owner). We recommend creating a separate service account for long-running ingestion jobs (service accounts should have scoped API key with only generation/embedding endpoints).
- API key scopes: staging: full (for smoke); prod: restricted to generate and embeddings only. No admin-level console keys should be stored in app config.
- Key rotation: recommend 30-day rotation for staged keys during validation, 90-day for production unless you require shorter. We support immediate rotation via API.
- Rate limit & batching: initial quota set to 50 RPS, with autoscale trigger at 70% sustained. We’ll watch KV cache hit rates and recommend batching config after 48h of traffic.
- Terraform snippet: we can seed projects via infra-as-code. I’ll paste the snippet in the kickoff doc.

Attachments we’ll post during the call: sample Terraform module, access-matrix.xlsx (filled), and the PO template.

Dev Patel
Implementation Engineer | Redwood Inference
